applied_additions.rationale: User call: the gates mostly create difficulties. Candidates are mold-cook-approval, mold-cook-handoff, cook-preparation-result, handoff-pointer, normalization-receipt, and phase-contract; approvals become wheypoint decision entries.
applied_additions.summary: Gates are the first cut; re-add any gate later only on demonstrated need.
Is the ontology one Record contract with typed entry kinds (requirement, criterion, decision, piece, finding, question), or separate Spec, Plan, and Review contracts linked to the backbone?
Does the delivery plan fold into the Plan as optional pr_group, branch, and stack_order fields on pieces, with no grouping meaning one PR?
Which survival test decides public contracts: A (an LLM writes and code reads), B (a durable artifact), or C (either)? The backbone directive may make this moot.
Do execution results fold into Plan piece status and evidence, and does diagnosis become a Review kind? Both are agent proposals the user has not confirmed.
Is the compiled per-task context a projection over the wheypoint graph (ADK style) or a ready-queue selection (Beads style)?
What sets plan weight (omitted, inline, or full): a code-scored complexity as in Taskmaster, or an agent or user choice as in OpenSpec lite?
Under a one-Record model, how do spec prose and diagrams fit, given the 6000-character notes cap and the parent's open living-spec fork?
How does one generator emit both the agent writer view and the host-complete shape for each kind, per the wiki consolidation audit?
Does any external reader consume schemas.easy-cheese.dev, and do removed contract URIs need a deprecation path?
Do the fan-out-bound contracts (remediation-state, remediation-cure-observation, review-request, diagnosis-request, pr-plan) leave with the stack, pending the parent's fan-out fork?

applied_additions.quote: There are fair amount of gates that mostly create difficulties, so I think those are the first to go. We can re-add them later.
applied_additions.summary: Cut the gates first; they can come back later.

applied_additions.quote: The high-level things that drive us are clearly wheypoint as the backbone, then specs, implementation plans, delivery plans, review-results i guess.
applied_additions.summary: The wheypoint is the backbone; specs, implementation plans, delivery plans, and review results are the high-level drivers.

applied_additions.quote: I think  we want to try to unifiy this in a way that doesnt force us to go through a bespoke mold cook age cure workflow (as pointed out in the previous wheypoint).
applied_additions.summary: Unify the artifacts so that work does not have to pass through the bespoke mold-cook-age-cure workflow.

applied_additions.quote: ontology of records, which may have verying degrees of specs and decisions (depending on the size) - prototypes, specs, reviews, whathaveyou, they all get cooked using a curd plan (which cna be as simple as inline, or omitted if its trivial)
applied_additions.summary: Treat objects as context compilation: an ontology of records of varying weight (prototypes, specs, reviews), each cooked through a curd plan that is inline or omitted when trivial.
